What to look for

This shader is not expected to compile. The question is *how* it fails, and
the two DXC panes fail differently -- that difference is the finding.

DXC 1.6.2112 (the older pane): a normal compile error, with a file, a line
and a column, naming the member that could not be found on the buffer type.
Whether that diagnostic is *right* is the original complaint; what matters
here is that it is an ordinary diagnostic.

DXC trunk (the newer pane): no diagnostic at all. Instead an internal
compiler error -- a message about a bad cast inside the compiler itself, and
a non-zero, non-standard exit status. There is no file, line or column,
because the front end never got the chance to complain: the compiler failed
inside code generation.

So read the panes for the *shape* of the failure, not for whether they are
red:

  - old pane: has a source location, has a diagnostic, exit status is the
    compiler's ordinary failure code
  - new pane: has neither, and reports an internal error

If a Clang pane is present, it is there to answer a different question --
whether the successor front end supports this spelling at all -- and an
unrelated "undeclared identifier" style error from it means only that the
feature is not implemented there yet, not that this issue is fixed.

The supported spelling (assign the subscript to a local variable, then call
the method on that local) compiles cleanly in every DXC that has the
feature; that control is in the triage directory, not in this link.
